thread: Folarin Balogun scored twice for USA vs Paraguay. Arsenal sold him for the wrong reasons — but don't get carried away.
The brace came in a transition-heavy setup with open space. That system doesn't exist at most top clubs. Arsenal didn't mismanage him. They misread his type.
Instinct 8 — elite finisher in open play. IQ 6 — drifts and disappears in possession. Gravity 7 — stretches lines but needs space. Transferability: 60%.
60% means: survives a move to the right system. Collapses in a possession-dominant side. Would you build a top-four attack around him?

instinct.evidence: Finds the net before defenders recover. Clinical in open play.

iq.evidence: Drifts and loses shape in possession. Becomes invisible in structure.

gravity.evidence: Pace stretches defensive lines — but only when given space to run into.

beats.claim: Folarin Balogun scored twice for the USA. That does not mean what you think.
beats.tension: Everyone is celebrating the Arsenal redemption arc. Nobody is looking at the system he scored in. Those goals came in a transition-heavy setup with open space. Change the structure and those goals do not happen.
beats.evidence: Instinct: eight. In open play his movement and finishing are elite — he finds the net before defenders recover. IQ: six. In possession-heavy systems he drifts, loses structure, becomes invisible. Gravity: seven. His pace stretches defensive lines and creates depth, but only when given space to run into.
beats.reveal: Transferability: sixty percent. That survives a move. But only to the right system. A transition-heavy side works. A possession-dominant top-four club collapses this. Arsenal did not mismanage him — they misread his type.
beats.loop: Would you build a top-four attack around a sixty percent transferability striker?
